gloss: start of winter; first day of winter

definitions.gloss: start of winter; first day of winter
definitions.explanation: one of the 24 solar terms ({二十四節気|にじゅうしせっき}) in the traditional East Asian calendar, marking the beginning of winter, usually falling around November 7-8

examples.japanese: {立冬|りっとう}を{過|す}ぎると{朝晩|あさばん}{冷|ひ}え{込|こ}む。
examples.english: After the start of winter, mornings and evenings become quite cold.

examples.japanese: {立冬|りっとう}の{日|ひ}に{鍋料理|なべりょうり}を{食|た}べるのが{我|わ}が{家|や}の{恒例|こうれい}だ。
examples.english: Eating hot pot on the first day of winter is a tradition in our family.

examples.japanese: {暦|こよみ}の{上|うえ}では{立冬|りっとう}を{迎|むか}えたが、{今年|ことし}はまだ{暖|あたた}かい{日|ひ}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: On the calendar we've reached the start of winter, but this year warm days still continue.

notes:
One of the {二十四節気|にじゅうしせっき} (24 solar terms). Falls around November 7-8, marking the calendrical start of winter. Like {立秋|りっしゅう}, the actual weather may not yet feel wintry at this time. The phrase {暦|こよみ}の{上|うえ}では (according to the calendar) is often used to acknowledge the gap between the calendar date and actual weather.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {立冬|りっとう}を{迎|むか}える: to reach the start of winter
- {立冬|りっとう}を{過|す}ぎる: to pass the start of winter
- {立冬|りっとう}の{候|こう}: seasonal greeting phrase for this time of year
- {暦|こよみ}の{上|うえ}では{立冬|りっとう}: calendrically it is the start of winter

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {立春|りっしゅん}: start of spring (around February 4)
- {立夏|りっか}: start of summer (around May 6)
- {立秋|りっしゅう}: start of autumn (around August 7)
- {冬至|とうじ}: winter solstice — the shortest day of the year, distinct from the start of winter
